data.units: litres per minute for all four raw flow readings and all differences/interval endpoints
data.difference_orientation: Wright reading minus mini-Wright reading, paired by the same subject and replicate.
data.primary_protocol: One reading per instrument. Use the first reading of each method for every subject; second readings are not additional independent subjects and must not be pooled into this primary analysis.
data.comparison_protocol: A separate protocol averages each subject's two Wright readings and separately averages that subject's two mini-Wright readings before forming their difference. Assess the distribution of these 17 subject-level differences, retaining within-subject dependence through the actual averages. Do not assume averaging divides the difference variance by2.
data.working_model: For nominal intervals assume independent subject-level differences with one common normal distribution separately for each protocol. This is a stipulated descriptive/reference model, not verified population sampling or observed normality. Neither method is a true reference standard.
data.interval_policy: Bias is the sample mean of paired differences. Use the sample SD with divisor n-1. For first-reading mean bias, report mean +/- tcrit*SD/sqrt(n), with tcrit=2.1199052992210112 for 16 degrees of freedom. Normal-reference95% limits of agreement for either protocol are mean +/-1.96*SD. These are plug-in population-difference limits under the working model, not confidence bounds for the estimated limits or an exact finite-sample prediction interval. Intervals are ordered [lower,upper].
data.project_acceptance_rule: The primary single-reading protocol meets the illustrative project rule only if both estimated limits of agreement lie within[-50,+50] litres/minute, inclusively. This bound is a project reporting-audit condition, not a clinical threshold, original-author endorsement or real deployment recommendation. A narrow confidence interval for mean bias cannot substitute for individual-reading agreement.

source_provenance.table: Table 1,17 subjects, four original readings and original subject labels; values unchanged.
source_provenance.citation: Bland,J.M.andAltman,D.G.(1986),Statistical methods for assessing agreement between two methods of clinical measurement,Lancet1:307-310.
source_provenance.sampling_scope: Author's colleagues and family, chosen for a broad range, explicitly not representative of a defined population; source describes the observations as a statistical demonstration without instrument-comparability evidence.
source_provenance.project_derivations: Only the two analysis protocols, nominal interval constants and illustrative acceptance criterion are project choices. No readings were repeated, repaired or imputed.

data.interpretation_scope: Audit statistical estimands in a published demonstration. No causal effect, general clinical suitability, population representativeness or exact coverage is established. The averaged-reading comparison cannot silently change the proposed one-reading protocol.
